findings.title: Closes #20 while its T-D3 limit is known broken
findings.description: The #87 description posted from this evidence says `Closes #20` in its first line, which makes GitHub close #20 when #87 merges. But #20's rewritten acceptance (`07-github-drafts.md`, section 2) requires at most 3 whole files per device per file per 60 s, and Qodo's open finding `feeaf5d4` (`06-final-state.md`) reproduces 5 whole-file sends in one window, so the closed ticket's criterion is not met.

citations.citation:
Closes #20

**PRD ID:** S1.5 · **Threat IDs:** T-D3

**T-D3 isn't fully closed: see #88.** Qodo's review of `d660eb6` found that refunds give back a share of pieces rather than bytes, so a stalled tail can allow more than 3 files' worth (`feeaf5d4`, open). The stopping rule for this PR's review rounds fired, so it's in #88 rather than fixed here.

## The new finding, recorded as unresolved
- **Where:** `web/index.html:83` (`refund`), with `check.js:153-210` and `peers.js:197-209`.
- **Qodo's claim:** `refund` gives back the *share of pieces* that didn't leave, but the budget is in *bytes*, and the last piece can be much shorter. For a 65,537-byte file, if the 65,536-byte first piece leaves and the 1-byte tail fails, half the charge is refunded. So a device can be sent almost the whole file again and again.
- **Checked [V]** with the real limiter at `d660eb6`, using `index.html`'s refund formula (`raw/28-qodo-new-finding-check.txt`): **5** whole-file asks were allowed in one window, 0.31 MB sent against a 0.19 MB budget. That's 5 files' worth against a limit of 3.
  - [A] In practice, the tail has to fail after the first piece leaves, for example on a stalled link.
- **Reproduction script:** `repro-feeaf5d4.mjs`, run as `node repro-feeaf5d4.mjs <c5>`.
- **Label: real.** It's reproduced with the real `askLimiter` and the real refund formula. The trigger, a short tail piece failing after a full piece left, was checked by reading `peers.js:197-209` (`sent` counts pieces, not bytes).

```markdown
### Summary
A device that keeps asking for the same file makes the sender upload it again and again, up to 200 MB each time (T-D3). It floods the room's relay and the sender's data.

### Acceptance (the attack fails)
- Per device and per file, the pieces sent in answer to its requests add up to at most 3 whole files in any 60 seconds. A `want` or a `need` with no list counts every piece, and a `need` with a list counts the pieces it lists. Every ask is charged at least one piece. Requests over the limit are dropped and nothing is sent. Pieces that were never sent are given back.
- A `need` with a list is allowed at most once a second per device per file. The receiver's own retries are 1.5–3 s apart, so they're never dropped.
- Dropped requests don't count towards the limit, so a device can't keep itself locked out.
- Requests for a file this device doesn't have, from a device that isn't in the room, or that ask for nothing (a `need` with an empty list, a print of size 0) are dropped before they're counted.

evidence.explanation: The PR body both auto-closes #20 and states that T-D3 is not fully closed, so the closing keyword attaches the tracker to a criterion the evidence shows is violated. The 5-vs-3 reproduction is recorded in the same PR, so the mismatch is documented but not reflected in the closing keyword.

findings.title: Unverified fixes can clear the merge gate
findings.description: The `mark-implemented` fallback directs the builder to close a finding after ten minutes even if Qodo has not re-attributed it, contradicting the policy's requirement that all three fix conditions hold. When a re-review leaves a finding open, that status write can release its merge-policy block without the required verification.

citations.citation:
## When a finding counts as fixed
All three must hold:
1. The finding is reproduced.
2. The fix is checked, with a test or a rerun.
3. Qodo's re-review on the new head re-attributes it.

## Resolver writes
- **`mark-implemented`:** If Qodo hasn't marked a reproduced, tested fix as implemented within 10 minutes of reviewing the head, I mark it myself.
- **`dismiss`:** the types are `intentional`, `false_positive` and `deferred`. Each needs its reason on the PR and the builder's OK.

Closing a finding is a **write** — it updates Qodo's review DB, restyles the finding's PR comments,
re-renders the review summary, and releases the merge-policy block that finding holds. Two commands,
and the distinction between them is the whole point: one says *the code changed*, the other says
*the code didn't and here's why*. Never use one to mean the other.

```
qodo pr-review-session mark-implemented --finding-ids <id>,<id> --explanation "what you changed" --json
qodo pr-review-session dismiss --finding-ids <id>,<id> --reason <reason> --explanation "why" --json
```

- **Batch per PR, one call.** Reconciliation runs once per call, not once per finding — so all the
  findings you implemented go in one `mark-implemented`, and all the ones sharing a dismissal reason
  go in one `dismiss`. Up to 100 ids.
- **`mark-implemented` only when explicitly authorized and for code you actually changed and pushed.** It clears the merge gate
  without a review having verified the fix, so a wrong claim ships an unfixed finding as fixed. If
  another review round is going to run anyway, prefer letting it re-attribute the fix itself; reach

evidence.explanation: The policy requires Qodo re-attribution as its third condition, then separately authorizes a manual `mark-implemented` when that has not happened. The resolver skill states that this write clears the merge gate without review verification.

location.code_snippet: +- **`mark-implemented`:** If Qodo hasn't marked a reproduced, tested fix as implemented within 10 minutes of reviewing the head, I mark it myself.

findings.title: Valid joins briefly show a failure message
findings.description: The proposed client-side timer shows “No match” after the 2-second pairing window, but `resolve()` can produce a valid `joined` result later than that. If the second device taps near the end of the window, the first device can show a failure before the time keeper pairs the taps and sends the successful layout.

citations.citation:
- Given two devices in a room, when each taps the join strip on facing edges within 2 s, then both show "Joined with <name>, on your right" (naming the other device and the side) and behave as one space.
- The two screens line up where the taps were: the point tapped on A's strip meets the point tapped on B's.
- Given a laptop and two phones, when the laptop taps its right strip **once for each phone**, at the point facing that phone, and each phone taps its left strip at the same moment, then both phones join, stacked down that edge.
- When a set of joins would leave screens overlapping (for example, both phones tapped the middle of their edge), the time keeper doesn't keep them and every device involved shows "Couldn't tell who to join. Try again".
- When only one device taps, or its tap is rejected (for example, sent just as the phone rotated), then after the 2 s window it shows "No match. Tap again together". The device that tapped starts its own timer, so this works even when the time keeper drops the tap without a `nomatch`.

evidence.explanation: `onPush` schedules resolution up to 900 ms after the latest push, and `resolve()` can retain an unmatched first push while its 2-second window remains open. A second, valid push near the end of that window can therefore be paired and broadcast only after the proposed local timer has displayed “No match.”

findings.title: Private code reaches Qodo without consent
findings.description: The `qodo-review` adapter permits implicit invocation, and the skill submits local diffs, untracked files, and session context to Qodo without requiring approval for that upload. During an ordinary coding task, an automatic checkpoint can therefore transmit unpublished source and notes even when the user has not requested an external review.

citations.citation:
default_prompt: "Use $qodo-review to review my local changes before I push them."
policy:
  allow_implicit_invocation: true

Review **local changes during coding and before handing off completed work**. `qodo review` sends your diff, new/untracked files and coding-session context to Qodo. Evaluate its structured findings and apply authorized fixes. Only the base commit must be on the remote; the command never pushes or creates a PR.

Use this skill for local changes, including unpushed work on an existing PR. Use `qodo-review-resolver` to work on findings from the PR's remote review; do not duplicate that review for an unchanged pushed snapshot.

## Prerequisites

- An authenticated Qodo CLI is available, or a connected QAR MCP server and a tested local input collector are available; review capability is enabled.
- The comparison base exists on the remote; local changes and context need not be pushed.
- The coding-session context and any ticket or design references are ready to attach.

## Checkpoints and final handoff

- Review a completed, testable slice when its feedback can guide the remaining work. Do not review
  unfinished exploration, every edit, trivial changes automatically, or simply because time passed.
  Respect the user's review scope and budget. A pause for a question or approval is not a final handoff.
- Keep at most one automatic checkpoint active per task. Retain its operation ID, submitted scope
  and snapshot/context association in the task's existing state. Poll status at natural pauses while
  doing useful work; do not launch another review to check progress or re-review unchanged inputs.

`qodo review` gathers, all client-side:

- The **tracked diff** vs the base, plus **new/untracked files** (secrets, binaries, oversized,
  and gitignored files are filtered out and reported — never silently dropped).
- The **branch name**, **HEAD commit**, and a **description** synthesized from your commit messages.
- Any **ticket refs** and **session context** you attach (below).

evidence.explanation: The new adapter enables implicit activation; the skill calls for automatic coding checkpoints and states that a review sends local changes and context to Qodo. Its prerequisites do not include approval for that disclosure.

findings.title: PR body says refunds work while a known bug remains
findings.description: The posted #87 body states that a send that did not leave is given back and that relay-dropped frames are refunded, which describes the piece-share refund in `refund` (`web/index.html:83`) that Qodo flags as over-refunding partial tails. A reader of the body would take the refund path as correct, even though the same body says T-D3 is not fully closed.

citations.citation: - **Refunds:** `allow` returns a token, and a send that didn't leave is given back (`undo`). `sendFile` resolves with `{ sent, of }` and marks failures the same way, so relay-dropped frames are refunded and an unknown error isn't.

evidence.explanation: The refund bullet presents the refund as correct, but Qodo's finding `feeaf5d4` (action_required, pending) says the refund gives back a fraction of pieces rather than bytes, so the description overstates what the code guarantees.
